Work starting to link A44 'bridge to nowhere' to road network

blocks.caption: A local industry lobby estimates economic costs of €200 million a year for as long as the A44 bridge remains unconnectedImage: Christoph Reichwein/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The notion of a bridge over the valley between Ratingen and Heiligenhaus to the east of Düsseldorf in western Germany as part of the A44 highway is more than half a century old. And the physical bridge itself has stood, complete, ever since 2022.
Yet still the crossing is not connected to any roads at either end.
A construction project to build the last 4.4 kilometers of highway and link the bridge to the A44 highway will formally start on Monday.
State premier Hendrik Wüst, as well as the regional transport and traffic ministers will attend the ground-breaking ceremony.
A project first conceived some 55 years ago has faced repeated delays because of lawsuits, environmental protection studies and onerous planning and permit procedures.

blocks.caption: Estimates suggest that once connected, around 36,000 vehicles would use the bridge dailyImage: Christoph Reichwein/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The bridge across the Angerbachtal (Angerbach Valley) should improve the road connection between the North Rhine-Westphalia state capital of Düsseldorf, the Bergisches Land mountain range and the industrial cities in the Ruhr Valley. It's also meant to help remove some strain from the perenially busy A3 highway and to improve the road connections to Düsseldorf International Airport.

The last stretch of highway is expected to cost around €200 million (roughly $220 million), or roughly the annual costs incurred each year by forcing traffic to divert around it, according to estimates from Düsseldorf's IHK industry and trade association.
Construction is expected to take several years, no formal end date has yet been set.
